analysis:
Examined the base text of MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift (lines 519-1435) and the supplied patch excerpt. The visible head change is in the text path: it adds a GenerationLoopExitThinkingPolicy.resolve call with a nil fallback when the bridge serves a distributed pair, passes exitThinking into GenerationLoopGuardPolicy.resolve, and hoists stopStringScope into a local. The patch excerpt is truncated, so changes beyond head line ~1108 are not visible, including the new range 1108-1169 and 1172-1173.

Security-relevant observations:
- The change touches generation-loop termination behavior only. It does not touch the encryption/decryption boundary, cacheScope/cacheSalt plumbing (T-041), attestation, authorization, or billing paths visible in the supplied text. cacheScope and cacheEnabled are still passed unchanged in the visible submitTokenized call.
- The media paths (VLM, cluster GLM/Qwen/MiMo) are base-only context and show no head changes in the visible ranges. The hoisted stopStringScope value is computed identically to the prior inline call.
- The new exitThinking logic inspects promptTokens and the tokenizer locally, so no new data exposure is visible. The availability/DoS angle (T-010, T-029) is improved if anything, since loops end the thought rather than burning the full max_tokens budget. Whether the exit-thinking injection could alter billed token counts or let a consumer-influenced prompt steer output is unverified, because the policy implementation is not supplied.

Remaining uncertainty: the truncated patch for head lines 1108-1173, which may modify the stream/event handling, and the implementation of GenerationLoopExitThinkingPolicy and the loop guard (injected tokens, reasoning-channel handling, usage accounting). A deeper pass should check that injected tokens cannot leak withheld reasoning or desync usage and billing signals.
